subject: Mop-up lanes and rollback runway for temporary dedicated reservation

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mop-up lanes and rollback runway for temporary dedicated reservation

Team —

We need a short-lived dedicated reservation for Acme Health to run a final round of heavy QA and productionization tests the week of July 9. This is a last-minute ask from their SREs: roughly 80 V100-equivalent slots for 36 hours (2x 18-hour windows) to validate failover and KV-cache warmup across our new routing policy.

A few specific asks from Product:
- Can Ops set up an "escrow" reservation we can hand back automatically if utilization drops below 10% for two consecutive one-hour windows?
- We need an autoscale policy exception so the reservation is not preempted for the duration, but with a circuit-breaker if queuing latency exceeds 2s for more than 10 minutes.
- Define a rollback runway: if the fallback model ramp triggers >25% error increase vs baseline, we automatically wind down the reservation and fail to regional standby.

Constraints: procurement needs a short SOW and formal quote before we can start billing; procurement@acmehealth.com is copied and expects an Ops-owned cost estimate by EOD Tue 6/25.

I've attached a sketch (Q3_mop_plan.xlsx) with traffic profiles and suggested windows. Can Ops and Infra weigh in with a minimal safe config, expected risk, and an ops checklist for cutover and rollback?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Infra Experiences
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mop-up lanes and rollback runway for temporary dedicated reservation

Kimberly —

We can accommodate a temporary carve for the July 9 window. Quick notes after an initial capacity check:
- 80 V100-equivalent slots for 36 hours is feasible in us-west-2 but requires taking a small preemptible buffer out of the shared pool for the preceding 48 hours to ensure warm caches.
- We can implement an "escrow" lease: reservation will be created with a utilization watcher that releases the reservation if average utilization < 10% for 2 consecutive 1-hour windows. That requires a small telemetry hook (we can stand this up in ~12 hours).
- Autoscale exception: we can flag the reservation as non-preemptible for the duration. Circuit-breaker: we can route new requests to standby region if p99 queue latency > 2s for 10 minutes. Implementation effort: ~2 engineer-days (runtime + routing).

Risks / trade-offs:
- Holding capacity reduces burst capacity for other pilots; Ops will need sign-off from Capacity Stewardship (I've looped Jonas).
- If fallback triggers, rolling back quickly will require a coordinated cache rehydrate plan to avoid cascade cold starts.

I'll draft a minimal ops checklist (cutover, smoke tests, failure scenarios) and a cost estimate by EOD Tue. If Procurement at Acme needs a formal quote earlier, let me know and we can escalate to sales to produce a PO quicker.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mop-up lanes and rollback runway for temporary dedicated reservation

Adding capacity perspective:

We can grant a temporary carve if product covers the proactive guardrails. Proposed technical guardrails:
1) Reservation escrow: automatic release criteria as Marcus described.
2) Circuit-breaker with graceful drain: when p99 queue > 2s for 10 minutes we start draining new sessions from the reservation and shift 20% traffic per 2 minutes to standby region, up to 100% over 10 minutes.
3) Pre-warm window: reserve an additional 8 hours before the start to pre-warm KV caches (will count toward the booking hours).
4) Fairshare compensation: we need an approved fairness credit to offset latency-sensitive tenants impacted during the reserved window. This should be included in the cost estimate.

Operationally, we request:
- A single oncall (Ops) owner for the window and a runbook with escalation tree.
- Product to sign off on rollback criteria in writing and to confirm which model variants are permitted as fallback.

If everyone agrees, I'll schedule the maintenance reservation and link the runbook to the ticket (INF-4532).

—Jonas
Senior Manager, Capacity Engineering
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Mop-up lanes and rollback runway for temporary dedicated reservation

Thanks — from Product's side we approve the guardrails above provided Procurement gets the cost breakdown. A couple clarifications:
- Fallback model variants: only quantized 7B family and the verified 13B slow-ram option are approved. No experimental weights.
- Rollback trigger: add a data-quality check alongside error-rate delta. If QA sample mismatch > 3% vs baseline in any of the three key prompt families, trigger rollback.

Procurement: Acme, can you confirm you will sign a purchase order for the reservation and the pre-warm hours? We do not start the pre-warm until PO is received.

I'll attach a short SOW draft in the Drive link and will update once legal has a line or two.

Thanks — Laura

Marta / Acme team —

Attached is a concise quote and SOW draft (temporary-reservation-policy-draft.md) and a line-item cost table: 80 slots x 32 billed hours (includes 8-hour pre-warm) = 2,560 slot-hours at the reserved pilot rate; refund policy: pre-warm hours are refundable if escrow releases before pre-warm completes, otherwise prorated refund for remaining unused hours. Escrow release due to low utilization will trigger a prorated refund for unconsumed hours.

Operational commitments: we will provide a runbook and a single Ops lead during the window, and the rollback will be executed automatically by the routing policy with manual override available to the oncall.

If Acme signs the PO by EOD Wed 6/26 we can lock the reservation and start the 8-hour pre-warm on Thu 7/8 at 22:00 PT.
